title: Firehall Meal Prep Ideas
subtitle: Cook once on a slow day — feed the loud ones
description: Firehall meal prep ideas: batch chili, sheet-pan components, pulled pork, and rice bases that reheat clean on busy shifts.
intro: Meal prep at a station means cooking components when the board is quiet so busy nights are assembly, not invention. Firehall meal prep ideas focus on proteins and sauces that reheat — not pre-plated meals that dry out.

sections.heading: Components that reheat clean
paragraphs: Chili, pulled pork, roasted chicken thighs, cooked rice, roasted veg. Combine into bowls, tacos, or bakes in under thirty minutes.

sections.heading: Label and rotate
paragraphs: Date everything, freeze what you will not use in three days, and post a fridge map so the next shift does not duplicate prep.

practicalAdvice: Prep proteins and sauces — assemble day-of.
Date and label everything — rotation prevents science experiments.
One prep cook, one list — avoid three people 'helping' differently.

mealRecommendations.title: Hall-Sized Beef and Bean Chili
mealRecommendations.blurb: Big pot Sunday — feeds the week.

faqs.question: Where do these recipes come from?
faqs.answer: Each link goes to a full recipe on Firehall Meals — crew-sized portions, station timing, and steps written for a shared kitchen. Not home-blog scaling.

faqs.question: What if crew size or time changes tonight?
faqs.answer: Use Find a Meal with your headcount and minutes available. It pulls from the same hall-tested dinners these guides recommend.
